chapter: Riddick band and the Fern dances
title: Waltzes at the Fern and Sharkey's band
summary: Sal talks about waltzes, and then praises Sharkey's band with Sidney Arodin, Harry Shields, Freddie Newman, Schellang and Caprera.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Oh man, the piano player had a big chord in front, you couldn't think that quick, you know, like waltzes would be like an A flat or B flat or B flat or A flat, when it was, you go right into a waltz, see, usually, Let Me Call Your Sweetheart or Girl Of My Dreams or, there wasn't too much of a right to waltzes. We would play, you know, just one every fourth piece would play, and the band would take a rest, see, and then the piano player would play, and then, see, on the other tune, played, this tune goes shocked, played all the time. What was the tune again? Oh, the sensation. No, it ain't the sensation. Play a little bit more. I can't. Oh man, Sharka played it all the time. I still love these Sharka, at the ringside, man. With Sidney Ira, man. He was the Sidney, huh? I never met him, he died. Played fine clarinet, man. Played fine clarinet. Sidney Ordon. Real French friends, man. What way? He could play some sticks, man. Boy, you know what? We were playing, we had to play on Tony Dalkyter. Tony Dalkyter. Tony Dalkyter. Yeah. He had to play Oakland Clare in it, man. Played fine Clare in it. Sidney Ardon. Real French friend, man. What way? He could play some sticks, man. Boy, you know what? When we were playing, we'd play at the park on Tony's Almarie kind of into an Almarie inside, man. They ain't shocking to play until we get off. They played us both low in there. I'd tell you, boy, Sharky was great, man. Sharky can't play like he played that. Sharky on trumpet, man. Sid Ardon. Harry Shields. Freddie Newman. August Schellinger on drums. And Joe Caprera, man. That band used to rock like that, man. They're one of the things Sharky's got. Solid, man. My boy, I think Sharky's great.

Did you ever play underneath Hawaiian skies? You know that, uh... Foozie Rye's about the only one I know around that knows it today. If I hear it, what? Raymond knows it. If she'd turn the machine off, I'd try to sing it. Mm-hm.
